ucs.title: [LLM] MuddyWater (Mango Sandstorm / TA450) remote-monitoring-tool drop after phishing-link click
ucs.description: Hunts MuddyWater's signature initial-access chain since 2023: spearphish with a link to a file-share-hosted installer for a legitimate Remote Monitoring & Management tool (ScreenConnect/ConnectWise, Atera, Syncro, RemoteUtilities, SimpleHelp), executed by the recipient and used as the C2 channel in place of custom malware. The detection ties an EmailEvents/UrlClickEvents recipient identity to an RMM agent process starting on their endpoint within a short window.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as command_line values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process values(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe","AteraAgent.exe","atera_setup.exe","Syncro.exe","Syncro.Service.Runner.exe","RemoteUtilities.exe","rutserv.exe","rutview.exe","SimpleHelp.exe","JWrapper-Remote Access.exe","kabuto.exe","RPort.exe","MeshAgent.exe") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.dest 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` 
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` 
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` 
| join type=inner host [
    | tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where Web.http_user_agent IN ("*ConnectWise*","*ScreenConnect*","*AteraAgent*","*RemoteUtilities*","*Syncro*") OR Web.url IN ("*screenconnect*","*pubnub.com*","*atera.com*","*syncromsp.com*","*rmansys.ru*","*remoteutilities.com*","*simple-help.com*") by Web.src 
    | rename Web.src as host
  ]
| eval ttp="MuddyWater / Mango Sandstorm RMM-as-C2 — T1219.002"
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let Lookback = 7d;
let WindowSec = 1800;
let RmmBinaries = dynamic(["ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe","AteraAgent.exe","atera_setup.exe","Syncro.exe","Syncro.Service.Runner.exe","RemoteUtilities.exe","rutserv.exe","rutview.exe","SimpleHelp.exe","JWrapper-Remote Access.exe","kabuto.exe","RPort.exe","MeshAgent.exe"]);
let Phish = EmailEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
    | where UrlCount > 0
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress, NetworkMessageId, Subject;
let RmmStart = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where TargetProcessName has_any (RmmBinaries) or ActingProcessName has_any (RmmBinaries)
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
RmmStart
| join kind=inner Phish on $left.ActorUsername == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| where ProcTime between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ProcTime, EmailTime)
| project EmailTime, ProcTime, DelaySec, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, SenderFromAddress, Subject, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, SHA256
| order by EmailTime desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: MuddyWater Mango Sandstorm RMM Tool Execution
id: 8f2c4b9a-3d51-4f8e-9c4b-1a2e3d4f5b6c
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of remote-monitoring-and-management tools repeatedly abused by MuddyWater / Mango Sandstorm / TA450 in place of custom malware after a spearphish.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2023/04/18/mercury-and-dev-1084-destructive-attack-on-hybrid-environment/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0069/
author: SOC detection engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1219.002
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.g0069
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
      - '\ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe'
      - '\ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe'
      - '\AteraAgent.exe'
      - '\atera_setup.exe'
      - '\Syncro.exe'
      - '\Syncro.Service.Runner.exe'
      - '\RemoteUtilities.exe'
      - '\rutserv.exe'
      - '\rutview.exe'
      - '\SimpleHelp.exe'
      - '\kabuto.exe'
      - '\RPort.exe'
      - '\MeshAgent.exe'
  filter_user:
    User|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection_img and not filter_user
falsepositives:
  - Sanctioned IT-helpdesk deployments of the same RMM software — pre-baseline known binary hashes per environment.
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe OR *\screenconnect.clientservice.exe OR *\SCREENCONNECT.CLIENTSERVICE.EXE OR *\ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe OR *\ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe OR *\AteraAgent.exe OR *\ateraagent.exe OR *\ATERAAGENT.EXE OR *\atera_setup.exe OR *\Syncro.exe OR *\syncro.exe OR *\RemoteUtilities.exe OR *\remoteutilities.exe OR *\rutserv.exe OR *\RUTSERV.EXE OR *\rutview.exe OR *\SimpleHelp.exe OR *\simplehelp.exe OR *\kabuto.exe OR *\RPort.exe OR *\rport.exe OR *\MeshAgent.exe OR *\meshagent.exe) -@User:*$
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(ScreenConnect\.(ClientService|WindowsClient|ClientSetup)|AteraAgent|atera_setup|Syncro(\.Service\.Runner)?|RemoteUtilities|rutserv|rutview|SimpleHelp|kabuto|RPort|MeshAgent)\.exe$/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)
ucs.rationale: MuddyWater pivoted almost entirely off custom-implant first-stage and onto signed, trusted RMM agents (ScreenConnect, Atera, Syncro, RemoteUtilities, SimpleHelp) post-2020 — documented by Microsoft (Mango Sandstorm / MERCURY), Mandiant, Group-IB and Proofpoint (TA450). Their phishing wave in late 2023 against Israeli orgs used trial-account Atera and Syncro installers hosted on Dropbox / OneDrive

ucs.title: [LLM] MuddyWater PowGoop side-loader: GoogleUpdate.exe loading goopdate.dll outside its trusted Google directory
ucs.description: Hunts the PowGoop loader family attributed to MuddyWater by Mandiant, Microsoft (Mango Sandstorm) and PaloAlto Unit 42: a legitimate Google Updater binary (GoogleUpdate.exe) dropped to a non-standard path is forced to side-load a malicious goopdate.dll, which then decrypts and runs an encrypted PowerShell stage from a config file shipped alongside it. Detects the signed-binary masquerade + DLL search-order hijack on the image-load telemetry, before the PowerShell stage runs.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as command_line values(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.parent_process_path) as parent_path values(Processes.process_hash) as parent_hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name=GoogleUpdate.exe AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_path 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` 
| where NOT match(parent_path, "(?i)\\\\Program Files( \(x86\))?\\\\Google\\\\") 
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` 
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` 
| eval ttp="MuddyWater PowGoop side-loader — T1574.002 + T1059.001"
ucs.kql:
let Lookback = 14d;
let GoogleTrusted = dynamic([@"c:\program files\google\", @"c:\program files (x86)\google\"]);
let SideLoads = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "GoogleUpdate.exe"
    | where FileName =~ "goopdate.dll" or FileName =~ "goopdate.dat" or FileName =~ "goopdate.res"
    | where not (tolower(FolderPath) startswith "c:\\program files\\google\\" or tolower(FolderPath) startswith "c:\\program files (x86)\\google\\")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, DllPath = FolderPath, DllName = FileName, DllSHA256 = SHA256;
let PsChildren = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "GoogleUpdate.exe"
    | where not (tolower(InitiatingProcessFolderPath) startswith "c:\\program files\\google\\" or tolower(InitiatingProcessFolderPath) startswith "c:\\program files (x86)\\google\\")
    | where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
          or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("goopdate","config.txt","-EncodedCommand","FromBase64String","IEX")
    | project ChildTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ChildImage = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256;
SideLoads
| union PsChildren
| project-reorder Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let Lookback = 14d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ActingProcessName has "GoogleUpdate.exe"
| where not (tolower(ActingProcessName) has @"\program files\google\" or tolower(ActingProcessName) has @"\program files (x86)\google\")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
      or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("goopdate","config.txt","-EncodedCommand","FromBase64String","IEX","Invoke-Expression")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: MuddyWater PowGoop GoogleUpdate.exe Side-Load From Non-Trusted Path
id: 7d3a1c2b-6e85-49d2-b3a4-c5d6e7f8a912
status: experimental
description: Detects MuddyWater's PowGoop loader — the legitimate signed GoogleUpdate.exe binary running from outside the standard Google Program Files directory and spawning a script-host child (PowerShell/cmd/rundll32) or referencing the PowGoop config artefact.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/powgoop-mercury-iranian-apt/
  - https://www.mandiant.com/resources/blog/mandiant-iran-uplevels
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0069/
author: SOC detection engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.g0069
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\GoogleUpdate.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  filter_trusted_path:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - ':\Program Files\Google\'
      - ':\Program Files (x86)\Google\'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and not filter_trusted_path
falsepositives:
  - Portable/sideloaded Chrome installations in dev environments — should be rare and named accordingly.
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\GoogleUpdate.exe OR *\googleupdate.exe OR *\GOOGLEUPDATE.EXE) -@ParentImage:(*\Program?Files\Google\* OR *\Program?Files?(x86)\Google\*) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\RunDll32.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^googleupdate\.exe$/i
| NOT ParentImageFileName=/\\Program Files( \(x86\))?\\Google\\/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|rundll32|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/goopdate|config\.txt|-EncodedCommand|FromBase64String|IEX|Invoke-Expression/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)
ucs.rationale: PowGoop is a MuddyWater-exclusive loader family — Unit 42 (Mango Sandstorm/MERCURY), Mandiant and ClearSky have all attributed the GoogleUpdate.exe + goopdate.dll + config.txt triplet to G0069. The side-load runs the signed Google binary from staging paths like %APPDATA%, %TEMP% or C:\ProgramData, so a parent-path negative-match on the two real Google install dirs combined with a script-host child
